properties.name: A what-if says what losing a premise costs a conclusion that is already contested, and names an objection that comes back when its reply loses support
properties.source: @ajs, 2026-10-18: "Capture the shortcomings (gaps) from the trial" (cogito trial)
properties.statement:
propagate_from on a premise says, per route, what the conclusion loses, even when the conclusion already reads unknown or contested (for example "route B loses its last unobjected premise"). It also names every objection that comes back into force because the reply that answered it lost its support: reinstatement in reverse.
Observed in the cogito trial (2026-10-18): losing con:def-thought reached 29 nodes, but req:i-exist "did not change, because it was already unknown". The walking objection, whose reply rested on that premise, showed up only as a "risk crossing", not as coming back.
